document: Changes from the SfM original measurement to the reconstruction

common.source_type: KIRI Engine scan (structure from motion), textured triangle mesh
common.reconstruction_type: procedurally generated model from idealised LEGO bricks, not a smoothed scan mesh
common.texture: no scan texture carried over; colours as material colours; for the figure additionally painted textures for head and torso

model_1.name: White stepped pyramid with 1x1 column and minifigure

problems: Flat ground surface and base of the scan untidy
Figure on top deformed and stretched (about 38 scan units high in the scan)

intermediate_cleanup.description: First round: scan only cleaned, not reconstructed
intermediate_cleanup.user_feedback: too heavily smoothed; wish: reconstruct from real bricks

structure.column: 5 bricks 1x1 stacked, position approx. (-P/2, -P/2) in stud units

reconstruction.method: Each level is divided into 2x2 blocks and tiled with 2x4 and 2x2 bricks by random domino tiling (best of 400 attempts, maximum number of 2x4); studs only where the next level does not rest on top
reconstruction.stud_visibility: Studs of covered cells are omitted

figure.approach: modelled completely anew, dimensions of the original minifigure 1:1 and scaled by 2/3
parts: torso with chain-mail print, scarf, brooch, belt, tunic
head with eyes, brows, moustache, mouth
arms with sleeves and C-shaped hands

assumptions: Only 2x4, 2x2 and 1x1 bricks in white, as stated by the user
Hidden brick distribution is random and not read from the scan
known_deviations: Colours of cloak, hands and sleeves look slightly paler than in the photos
Chain mail as a honeycomb pattern instead of individual rings

model_2.name: Stepped pyramid with grey stair arms and temple

problems: Pyramid rotated by approx. 16° relative to the ground surface
Wavy ground surface, ground rises towards the pyramid
Scan compressed along one axis (approx. factor 0.72)
Stair side partly disintegrated in the scan

measurement.method: Alignment by histogram sharpness around the temple centre; height and colour map from 4 million surface points

v1.note: from scan dimensions, black stairs, superseded

temple.course_2: four white 1x1 corner pillars, hollow inside

white_block_yaw_deg.description: Slight rotation of the upper white corner blocks measured from the scan; each block rotates as a whole

decisions_by_user_feedback: Stairs and white corners according to the photo: all steps one stud wide, level 5 as 2x2
Four 1x1 pillars in the temple slightly rotated
assumptions: Seven levels according to the photo and the user's statement; the scan suggests rather 8 levels with 20x20 studs (lowest levels presumably merged with the table)
Rotation angles of the pillars estimated by eye from the close-up photo, rotation direction uncertain
Rotation angles of the upper white blocks from the compressed scan, approx. 20 % uncertainty
known_deviations: A few 1x2 and 1x4 bricks, because odd-sized corner areas would otherwise require many 1x1 bricks
Stair arms at levels 6 and 7 not quite symmetrical in the photo, symmetrical in the model
Ground surface of the scan not carried over
